headline: Morocco's upset would quietly crown a new favorite — just not Morocco
body: France enter at 68.7% to win this match, but the simulation data reveals a striking downstream effect if Morocco pulls off the 31.3% shot: Spain's title probability jumps from 25.3% to 29.8%, making Spain the biggest beneficiary of a French exit. Morocco's own title chance would rise from 3.6% to 12.2%, a significant leap, yet Spain would still sit ahead of them in the title race even in that scenario.

headline: Spain is the tournament's top-rated team — and Belgium faces the steepest climb
body: Spain's Elo of 2177 is the highest in the field, sitting 216 points clear of Belgium's 1961, and the simulations reflect that gap with Spain winning 69.3% of the time. Belgium's path to the title runs through a 30.7% chance here, and even then their title probability only reaches 16.6% — meaning the bracket beyond this match keeps their ceiling firmly in check.

headline: Norway vs England is the round's closest matchup by Elo, and penalties loom large
body: With just 104 Elo points separating Norway (1972) and England (2076), this is the smallest gap of any quarterfinal, and the model gives this match a 26.5% chance of reaching penalties — higher than any of the other three quarterfinals. England are favored at 60.7%, but the shootup scenario alone accounts for more than one-in-four simulations.

headline: England and France stand to gain almost as much from a Switzerland win as Switzerland does
body: If Switzerland's 31.8% chance materializes, their title probability climbs from 4.8% to 14.3% — but the ripple effects are nearly as consequential for others: England's title chance rises from 13.0% to 17.7% and France's from 20.0% to 22.3% with Argentina eliminated. Argentina enter as favorites at 68.2%, but a Swiss upset would reshape the entire SF2 bracket side, which currently holds a combined 46.1% title share.
